To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

antibodies to acetylchlorine receptors from Electrophorus electroplaques bind to the postjunction surface membrane of the electroplaques and that antibodies to acethylcholine receptors from Torpedo electroplaques bind specifically to the receptors on the surface of the vesicles prepared from Torpedo electroplaque membranes by subcellular fractions.

antibodies to the purified acetylcholinereceptor from the electric organs of Torpedo and Electrophorus bind specifically to the receptors in solution, in the membranes of intact electroplax, and in receptor-rich vesicles.
antibodies to acetyl-choline receptor bind to the receptor in solution as well as in the intact electroplasm and to receptor-rich subcellular vesicles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a sensitive, quantitative immunoprecipitaton procedure for the measurement of acetylcholino receptors and the application of the method to the analysis of receptor structure.
the development of an assay system to measure binding of antibodies to acethylcholine receptors in solution and in membrane preparations.
the development of methods for the preparation and study of acetylcholinerich membranes from Torpedo and Electrophorus electric tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antibodies raised against Torpedo and Electrophorus acetylcholine receptor bind to the receptor in solution, to the receptor in the membrane and to the receptor in isolated vesicles.
the binding of antibodies to the receptor is not a significant effect.

antibodies raised to purified receptor from one species bind to receptor in membranes from both the same and the other species, but that the antibodies raised in the rabbit to the Electrophorus receptor can block the response of the Electrophorus electrocyte to stimulation, while the Torpedo antisera have no effect on this system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antibodies to purified acetylcholinergic receptors can bind specifically to the receptor in situ and to receptor-rich vesicle preparations.
we have developed a method to visualize the receptor at the electron microscopic level.
the binding sites on receptor for antibodies are distinct from the binding sites on the receptor for acetylcholine and for alpha-neurotoxins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antibodies against the receptor can be used to study the receptor in the membrane.
the receptor is a very sensitive indicator of the receptor-mediated receptor.
the binding of anti- receptor antibodies can be detected on intact membranes and in membrane vesicles.
